themes_detail.label: Damaged Street Signs Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK versus 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting either acute infrastructure failure, vehicle collisions, or vandalism requiring urgent investigation.
evidence: 3 street sign damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Community Board repeatedly requests street light and infrastructure repairs, suggesting pattern of deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Site visit to identify which signs are damaged and whether pattern correlates to specific intersections or construction zones
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog and whether this reflects wider infrastructure deterioration in East Harlem

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Explodes
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints reached 3 LAST WEEK versus 0.1 weekly average—a 2300% spike with the highest z-score (8.69) in the dataset—indicating either organized tree removal, storm damage, or development-related activity requiring immediate explanation.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)—2300% increase
Highest z-score in entire dataset (8.69), indicating most statistically significant anomaly
Active ULURP rezoning at 58-62 East 125th Street and completed City Map change at The Beacon project could correlate with tree removal
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with recent development permits (433 filed in last 90 days) and active rezoning applications to determine if tree damage linked to construction
Interview Parks Department and residents to identify which trees were damaged, by whom, and whether permits were obtained

themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Complaints Double
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints reached 7 LAST WEEK versus 3.1 weekly average—a 124% spike (z-score: 4.18)—suggesting either increased cruelty, better reporting, or a concentrated incident requiring urgent investigation and animal welfare agency coordination.
evidence: 7 animal abuse complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.1 weekly average (8-week baseline)—124% increase
Z-score of 4.18 places this among top statistical anomalies
No community board or constituent case data available to corroborate, but signal is strong enough to warrant field reporting
reporting_angles: Obtain detailed 311 complaint narratives to determine if incidents are isolated cases or part of coordinated pattern
Contact ASPCA and NYC Animal Care and Control to cross-reference complaints with their incident logs and enforcement actions

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints jumped to 8 LAST WEEK versus 2.2 weekly average—a 256% spike (z-score: 4.8)—aligning with recurring community board requests for DOT infrastructure improvements and suggesting deferred maintenance creating safety hazards.
evidence: 8 sidewalk condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.2 weekly average (8-week baseline)—256% increase
Z-score of 4.8 ranks among top anomalies in dataset
Community Board budget requests repeatedly include 'park, building, or access improvements' from DOT—suggests long-running unmet need now accelerating
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints geographically to identify neighborhoods with worst sidewalk deterioration and photograph conditions
Interview residents and business owners about trip hazards and accessibility issues, particularly for elderly and disabled residents

themes_detail.label: Street Light Outages Rise
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints reached 14 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 3.6 weekly average—a 286% spike (z-score: 4.65)—directly mirroring a standing community board budget request for street light repairs and correlating with safety concerns in under-lit neighborhoods.
evidence: 14 street light condition complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 3.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)—286% increase
Z-score of 4.65 places this among significant spikes
Community Board has requested 'Repair or provide new street lights' from DOT for multiple budget cycles—chronic unmet need now spiking
reporting_angles: Request DOT data on street light maintenance backlog and timeline for repairs in East Harlem
Interview residents about how outages impact safety perceptions, street activity, and quality of life
